name: Good Morning, Shelf
creator: Operated by the Ward 6-7 Community Frequency Cooperative
description: A daily morning audio show broadcast on a low-power community frequency covering Wards 6 and 7 of the Shelf, running since 2191 and staffed entirely by rotating volunteer hosts from the local community. The show covers hyperlocal news — water access updates, community meeting announcements, missing persons notices, informal job listings, deaths and births — alongside music, listener call-ins, and occasional longer interviews with community figures. It has no production budget, frequently cuts out mid-broadcast when the transmitter fails, and is beloved with an intensity that better-produced shows rarely achieve.
medium: community radio frequency / local audio broadcast
cultural_impact: Good Morning, Shelf is frequently cited by Ward 6-7 residents as their primary source of information that actually pertains to their lives, predating and outlasting multiple corporate-funded 'community outreach' media projects targeting the Shelf demographic.
controversy: Municipal authorities have issued three cease-and-desist orders against the cooperative for operating an unlicensed broadcast frequency; each time, the show has gone silent for weeks and then resumed on a slightly different frequency. The fourth order, issued in 2219, is currently being contested.
story_hooks: A missing persons notice read on the show prompts a listener to call in with information that suggests the disappearance is connected to a corponation infrastructure project running under the ward — and suddenly the cooperative is under pressure to retract the notice.

One of the rotating hosts begins using their time slot to broadcast encoded information that regular listeners can't interpret but someone clearly can — and the cooperative's other members don't know whether to confront them or protect them.

The transmitter fails permanently during a broadcast about a community water contamination alert, and the cooperative has forty-eight hours to find a replacement before the information cycle moves on and the alert disappears.
